cards.explanation: The answer is eighteen, friends. Luke says she had been disabled by a spirit for eighteen years, hunched over and unable to stand up straight (Luke 13:11). That's a long, long time to carry that. I think eighteen years is worth slowing down for.

The answer is that Jesus calls her over to Him. Luke says, "When Jesus saw her, He called her over…" (Luke 13:12). He saw her, and He called her over. No waiting, no committee meeting. I think being noticed like that meant a lot.

The answer is True, friends. Jesus says, "Woman, you are set free from your disability." (Luke 13:12). Say it slowly, because eighteen years of bending came before those words. I think she heard every one of them.

The answer is immediately! Luke says, "Then He placed His hands on her, and immediately she straightened up…" (Luke 13:13). No waiting room, no follow-up appointment. Eighteen years of bending, and it took no time at all once His hands were on her.

The answer is that she begins to glorify God! Luke says she "…straightened up and began to glorify God." (Luke 13:13). First thing she does after eighteen years is give God the glory. I think that's the most beautiful thing she could have done with that first straight breath.

The answer is that Jesus healed on the Sabbath. Luke says the synagogue leader "…was indignant that Jesus had healed on the Sabbath." (Luke 13:14). A woman was set free, and the Sabbath is what he was upset about. I think I'd have been asking for a second look at my priorities.

The answer is False, friends. The leader "…told the crowd." "There are six days for work… So come and be healed on those days and not on the Sabbath." (Luke 13:14). He spoke to the crowd, not to Jesus. The text doesn't say why he chose to speak to them.

The answer is that each of them unties his ox or donkey from the stall and leads it to water. Jesus asks, "Does not each of you on the Sabbath untie his ox or donkey from the stall and lead it to water?" (Luke 13:15). The ox or donkey gets untied and led to water on the Sabbath. I think Jesus was making His point with something they already did.

The answer is False, friends. The leader was the one saying to come on the six days (Luke 13:14). Jesus asks, "Then should not this daughter of Abraham… be released from her bondage on the Sabbath day?" (Luke 13:16). He's saying she should be released on the Sabbath day.

The answer is True, friends. Jesus says Satan had kept her bound for "…eighteen long years…" (Luke 13:16). That's His own word for it, and He calls it her bondage. Then He says she should be released from it, and she was.

The answers are humiliated and rejoices. Luke says, "…all His adversaries were humiliated." (Luke 13:17). That's what the text says happened to them after Jesus spoke. It's the opposite of what happened to the crowd. Luke says, "…the whole crowd rejoiced at all the glorious things He was doing." (Luke 13:17). The whole crowd, not just a few, friends.
